# Itiha intelligence brief, 2026-11-24

**Guru Tegh Bahadur's date is today and his Short is not up yet: publish it by 17:00 IST. The Tipu Sultan Short lapsed this morning with nothing made, so its place goes to a Churchill Short for his birthday on 30 November. Long-form is drawing more viewers but fewer subscribers per view than it used to.**

## This week: 3 decisions
1. **Script and publish a Short on Aurangzeb's order to execute Guru Tegh Bahadur, for 24 November.** (short, due 2026-11-24, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: Today is the date, and it names Aurangzeb, the villain of the channel's two largest videos. His name is trending on X in India this morning, beside Guru Nanak Jayanti. Breakouts are furthest behind: 0 subscribers from them this month against 1,793 planned. It rests on the date, so judge it on search views over the year.  
   First step: Write it in this sitting: open on Sis Ganj in Chandni Chowk, then Aurangzeb's order as an act of state, not a martyr story. Title starts “Guru Tegh Bahadur”. Publish by 17:00 IST today.
2. **Script and publish a follow-up long-form for the Indonesia video's viewers: why Bali stayed Hindu when Java converted.** (long, due 2026-12-02, open since 2026-11-19)  
   Why: The Indonesia long-form brings 3.8 subscribers per 1,000 views against 2 for the bigger Asia one, and it beat the usual long-form last week. Its daily views are falling, so the follow-up should land while its viewers still arrive. The Bali topic is a guess from the comments.  
   First step: Put the Indonesia transcript in the long-form scripts folder today so its drop-off check can run; it is still missing. Then sources on Majapahit's fall and the priests who moved to Bali. Name a culprit and a date.
3. **Script and publish a Short for Churchill's birthday on 30 November: what his War Cabinet was told about the Bengal famine in 1943, and what it decided.** (short, due 2026-11-30, new)  
   Why: The next dated villain on the calendar: a ruler's own papers on a famine that killed Indians. The video that brings the most subscribers per view in the last 90 days, “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, won the same way, a villain convicted by his own record. His readership is at its usual level, so this rests on the date alone and is a guess.  
   First step: Nothing is on disk. Read the War Cabinet minutes and Leo Amery's diary for 1943 first. Open on the document and its date, one sentence of context at most: the last Churchill Short lost viewers in its first seconds.

Everything below is the evidence. Mark a decision done or dropped on the Brief tab; an open one stays here until then.

## Channel health
18,200 subscribers, up 600 in a week, against 100,000 by 28 September 2027. November's milestone is 20,508, which needs 79.1 net a day; the last 7 days ran at 103.9, faster than that, but the channel starts 1,797 behind the ramp, so on the 7-day rate the month ends near 18,823, 1,685 short. Only 49.1% of net subscribers over 28 days came from videos; the rest is tied to no video and can stop without warning. Furthest behind is breakouts, 0 against 1,793 this month; one video of the usual breakout size (1,396 subscribers) would close most of it. The Tipu Sultan Short lapsed today with nothing shipped and is not proposed again. Last week both uploads were the owner's own picks and none of the 58 recommendations shipped; the long-form beat the usual and the Short did not, so the list holds one dated Short at a time plus the long-form follow-up.

What's working
- “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus” carried long-form: long-form views rose 42.4% week over week, and the video has 101,761 views in 6 days. New long-forms have brought 598 subscribers this month against 104 planned, and over 28 days long-form earns 84.0% of the net subscribers videos bring.
- The video that brings the most subscribers per view in the 90-day window is still “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 11 net per 1,000 views. Its lesson: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.” The Churchill Short is built on it.
- “Why Is Ram Setu Called ADAM'S Bridge?” still draws views every day, nearly three weeks out, from searches such as “ram setu bridge” and “adams bridge”: 12,161 so far. A searched name in the title keeps a Short alive after the feed lets go, which is why the Tegh Bahadur title starts with his name.

What's wrong
- Long-form brings fewer subscribers per view than it used to: 7.4 per 1,000 over the 365-day window, below its usual range. The Ramayana videos pull it down: the Asia one brings 2 per 1,000 and the India one 1.1, and only 41.7% of November's long-form views were engaged. Probable cause: a story with no culprit gets played from the Home feed but not followed. Test: the Bali video names a culprit and a date; compare its subscribers per 1,000 on day three with the Indonesia one's.
- Viewers leave the long-forms early: the 7-day average view is down to 27.3%, and all three Ramayana long-forms lose most of their viewers in the first third. Probable cause: Home-feed plays that are not real viewing. Test: not possible on the Indonesia video until its transcript is in the scripts folder, the Bali decision's first step.
- Shorts views fell 80.8% week over week to 2026-11-21, and the Ramayana film has stopped carrying Shorts: “Every Ramayana Kept One Rule. The Ramayana Movie BROKE It” (15 November) has 1,761 views against 78,798 for the one of 11 November, though its viewers stayed. Probable cause: the film is in its third week and losing screens. Test: none needed; no more film Shorts, and dated Shorts take the slot.

## Audience
Analytics runs to 2026-11-21. Long-form is watched from the Home and subscription feeds (231,313 of 258,577 views over 28 days, against 6,574 from search). Shorts get 83,171 of their 28-day views from search, which is why a Short titled with a searched name keeps earning.
- The Indonesia video's corrections are specific and will come back for Bali: a viewer of Indonesian and Indian parents says the Allah-and-Ravana version is the Malay “Hikayat Seri Rama”, written in Jawi script, and an Indonesian viewer says Rama was not worshipped there in the Majapahit era. The Malay Short and the Bali script should say Malay where it is Malay, and check the Majapahit claim before recording.
- A Muslim viewer from Java is in the same thread explaining the Malay tradition, while much of the anger under the video is aimed at Islam as a whole. A follow-up that names a culprit and a date, not a religion, keeps viewers like him.
- itiha.info: Google still finds the site only by its name, and November's search impressions are lower again ([Search Console](https://search.google.com/search-console?resource_id=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.itiha.info%2F)). Site traffic cannot be read until the Analytics id is set (see actions).

## How they are reacting
The Indonesia long-form still holds the week's comments: corrections from Indonesian and Malay viewers, a long fact-check, and anger turning from the rewrite to Islam. Under the Sai Pallavi Short the complaint is that she played Sita and defended Ravana.
- **Corrections from viewers in the region** (mixed): "This particular version of the Ramayana you are mentioning is a Malaysian adaptation known as the Hikayat Seri Rama"
- **A fact-check of the Indonesia video** (negative): "Its striking facts are mostly real, but several supporting facts are wrong"
- **Anger turning on Islam as a whole** (negative): "Lol allah need ramayan to become popular"
- **Viewers abroad who grew up with the Ramayana** (positive): "I'm a Burmese and Buddhist from my home country Myanmar but still big fan of Ramayana"
- **Sai Pallavi playing Sita and defending Ravana** (negative): "The irony of playing Sita and defending Ravana in return"
- **Ravana's motive in the new film** (mixed): "they properly showed the arrogance part but replaced lust with revenge which leads to the controversy"

Requested topics
- A Krishna video in the shape of the Asia Ramayana one
- Bagan and Hindu influence in Myanmar
- Rajendra Chola's raid on Srivijaya (asked under the Asia video)
- Hindi versions of the long-forms

## Competitors
The month's top Shorts on the watchlist come from Hindu Lifestyle, a channel larger than Itiha, and both open by quoting the thing they are about to argue with. Elsewhere the Ramayana film still drives the big Shorts.
- **Hindu Lifestyle**: "Diwali is South Asian... wait.. what?"
  Why it worked: 161,137 views at 31x the channel's median. It opens on the other side's claim in their own words, “Diwali is not a Hindu festival. It's a South Asian festival”, then one word: “What?”
  Steal: For Churchill: open on the line his defenders use about the famine, in their words, then put the War Cabinet's own record against it.
- **Hindu Lifestyle**: "Boycott the Ramayana? What?"
  Why it worked: 111,725 views at 21.5x the median. The first sentence speaks to a plan the viewer already has: “If you plan on boycotting the new Ramayan movie, you might be doing more harm than good. Let me explain.”
  Steal: Speak to the viewer's own experience in sentence one. For Bali: if you have been there, you have seen a Hindu island in a Muslim country; here is why.
- **The Sham Sharma Show**: "Bali Death Dark Truth"
  Why it worked: 611,041 views at 4.2x his median, one of his run of Ramayana film Shorts. In Hindi, Bali is also Vali of the Ramayana.
  Steal: A warning for the Bali title: put Indonesia in it, or search may send it people looking for Vali. A guess, but a cheap one to avoid.

Gaps
- “Why Did Japan Make Indian Propaganda Posters?” (The Emissary, a Short) has no equivalent on the channel: two empires competing for the same Indian soldiers. See the second idea below.

## Trending now, make this
- **today, short, 3/5**: Guru Tegh Bahadur, today  
  Signal: Executed in Delhi in 1675 and remembered on 24 November. His name is trending on X in India and Guru Nanak Jayanti is the second trend, so Sikh history has the day's attention. The searched phrase is “guru tegh bahadur history”. No script is on disk. (Calendar, X trends, decision)  
  Make: Publish by 17:00 IST, under a minute, title starting with his name, Aurangzeb in the first sentence. Tell it as an order of state, not a martyr story. Judge it on search views over the year.
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: Winston Churchill's birthday, 30 November  
  Signal: Six days out; the recording step falls this week. His English Wikipedia readership is at its usual level, so this rests on the date alone. (Calendar, decision)  
  Make: Record by 27 November and publish on the morning of 30 November, his name first in the title. One document, its date, then what was decided.
- **watch, short, 1/5**: Two films on 4 December: Eetha and Maatrubhumi  
  Signal: Both are large releases with trailers out, Eetha a biopic with Shraddha Kapoor and Maatrubhumi a war film with Salman Khan. Neither has a confirmed historical subject in the data. (Moments radar (Wikipedia))  
  Make: Find out by 27 November what each is about. Only a real historical subject gets a Short, published 5 to 13 December, on the story the film leaves out.
- **watch, short, 3/5**: Bangladesh, 14 December 1971: the intellectuals killed  
  Signal: 20 days out; the research step falls on 30 November. A named perpetrator, the Pakistan Army and its local allies, and a date. (Calendar)  
  Make: Watch, not yet a decision. If it is made, the killing goes in the first sentence, named and dated: the channel's 1971 refugees video kept its cover-up for late and few saw it.
- **today, skip, 1/5**: Tarabai jails Rajaram II, 24 November 1750  
  Signal: On the calendar for today, and the channel's Tarabai Short is one of its biggest. (Calendar)  
  Make: Skip. It makes the heroine of that Short the jailer of the boy she put on the throne, and videos that cut down a figure the audience loves are the weakest group on this channel.
- **today, skip, 1/5**: Guru Nanak Jayanti  
  Signal: The second trend on X in India, and his English Wikipedia readership is at 2.06x its usual. (X trends, Wikipedia pageviews)  
  Make: Skip a separate Short: a saint's life has no culprit, and saint stories are among the weakest here. Let the Tegh Bahadur Short carry the day.

## Topic ideas (voltage-checked)
- [3/5, long] **Aurangzeb's Own Court Wrote Down the Temples He Destroyed**  
  Villain plus hypocrisy: his own court chronicle, the Maasir-i-Alamgiri, records the orders against the Vishwanath temple at Benares in 1669 and the Keshava Deva temple at Mathura in 1670; Contested history: the living argument that the Mughals did not destroy temples, which the channel's Irfan Habib Shorts already took on; Religion and identity stakes, with a named culprit and a dated act for the first sentence  
  source: Mohak Mangal's “Reality of Aurangzeb” ran well above his usual and nobody on the watchlist or on Itiha has the subject; read it from the chronicle, not from his video. Aurangzeb is the villain of the channel's two largest Shorts, but a long-form on him is a guess. It follows the Tegh Bahadur Short. Check every date before scripting.
- [2/5, short] **Why Japan Printed Posters for Indian Soldiers**  
  Empire mechanism: Japan and Britain competed for the same Indian soldiers during the Second World War; Hidden history: the posters are a record few viewers have seen  
  source: The Emissary's Short on it is among his top videos and Itiha has nothing like it. A guess here: freedom-movement Shorts have done poorly on this channel, so it opens on the poster and the two empires, not on a fighter's life.

## Instagram (separate platform, separate audience)
Instagram has 25,542 followers, up 166 in 7 days, 23.7 a day. The British officers' pay reel has reached 816 with a 59.0% skip rate, worse than the level breakout reels stay under. Carousels still do the growing: their median reach is 3.7x that of reels.

Do more
- Write carousels that correct the record  
  50 revision carousels in the band converted a median 53.5 followers against 20.5 for the other lanes (40 posts). Median reach 15.9k vs 10.9k, conversion 3.77 vs 1.95 per 1k. 477 followers a month at stake.
- Build every carousel at 7-10 cards  
  The median carousel in the 7-10 band converts 34.5 followers (90 posts); outside the band, 12 (16 posts). Pooled rate 2.89 vs 1.85 follows per 1k reach — the band is not just reaching more people, it converts better per person reached, so this is not a reach artefact. 420 followers a month at stake.

Do less
- Stop making posts that get shared without bringing followers  
  18 of 104 rated posts are shared above the median (24.7/1k) but convert below it (2.0/1k): median 9.8k reach for a median 9 followers. The 34 posts that do both average 275 followers each. Share rate and follow rate correlate at only 0.39 — shareable and followable are separate skills, and the first one flatters itself on the home screen. 918 followers a month at stake.
- Stop posting single images  
  87 single images all time: 84.2k reach between them and 120 followers, 1.4 per post. A carousel in the 7-10 band averages 159.6. Every image slot is a carousel slot not taken. 92 followers a month at stake.

## Housekeeping
- **this_week**: Upload the Malay Ramayana Short (Ravana getting his powers from Allah) on 25 or 26 November, title starting “Ravana”, the Indonesia long-form as its related video, and name the text as the Malay “Hikayat Seri Rama”.  
  The script is written from the owner's own draft and was made to send viewers to the Indonesia long-form. Commenters there have already said this version is Malay, so the Short should say so. That it sends viewers on is a guess.
- **this_week**: Test a new title and the designer's thumbnail on “The Church That Ran Britain's PRISON Camps” in Studio's Test & Compare.  
  Over the 365-day window it brings 34.3 subscribers per 1,000 views, the best on the channel, on only 1,078 views: the people who find it subscribe, and too few find it. That the title is the reason is a guess.
- **later**: Check in Studio why “How Jati's evolve organically ?” still has 19 views since 3 November.  
  A public Short gets at least a few views a day; this points to a visibility setting or a restriction, not the topic.
- **later**: Set GA4_PROPERTY_ID in .env so the brief can read itiha.info's traffic.  
  Search Console alone is thin: every query that shows is the brand name.
